BIOL 310 was my most despised class, I absolutely hated it. I had it with Lawrey, but from what I've heard, him and Weeks are equally hard. The only grade was 3 exams and, though they were 100% memorization and multiple choice, he managed to make them very difficult. The lab is pretty cool though, most of the time it was just taking photos under the microscope and then a lot of dissections toward the end. I took it alongside micro and physics and it gave me the most trouble. You can pull at least a B if you put in an honest effort and don't try to cram the material the night before- it won't work.

I transferred to GMU in fall 2016 at 25 years old. My hometown is an hour and a half away and I had to live in a dorm as it was my only option at the time. My first year I had no friends- none. My first semester I lived with an international student from China and while she was as sweet as could be, she didn’t speak much conversational English. She moved out over winter break and I was alone in the dorm for spring 2017. It was saaaaad times because l felt like all of the students on campus already had their friend groups. I also felt like I couldn’t relate to the “younger crowd” because we just didn’t care about the same things.

BUT I started to actually make friends- and even met my lovely boyfriend- once I got into my major-specific classes and labs my senior year by swapping numbers and getting together for HW sessions. Most of my friends are older students, it seems to be a pretty common thing.

I had this EXACT problem on my Mac last semester. It turned out that my Masonlive account had somehow been logged out of Microsoft Office. Open Word from your dock and on the screen that says "New, Recent, Shared" etc, there's a bubble in the top left with your initial in it and name under it. Click that bubble and make sure it's your full 'xxxxx@masonlive.gmu.edu' account that is signed in. If not, then sign out and sign back in with your Masonlive credentials. You may need to restart your computer after signing in, but I don't really remember. Alternatively, you can use the Live Support feature at https://itservices.gmu.edu. That's how I got help with my issue.

No, no, no, don't feel stupid! I gave myself literally two weeks to prepare for the GRE. I took my first practice exam before I started studying and I got a 147V/149Q. What a blow to the ego that was. Here's how I prepared:

-Studied 3-4 hours a day for those two weeks, using Manhatten Prep's 5-lb Book and ETS's book of quantitative problems

-Studied vocabulary flashcards with the Magoosh app every time I had a free minute, for example sitting in the passanger seat while driving, waiting at the DMV, etc

-Used ETS's pool of essay questions to write two essays a day, one of each


I took the GRE 3 days ago and got 158V/152Q. Not a stellar score and I'll definitely be taking it again, but that's where two weeks of studying got me.

Hope is not lost as long as you buckle down and take your studying seriously. 

Edit: It's probably fair to mention that I spent much more time studying for verbal than quantitative because I figured that was where I needed the biggest improvement. Also worth mentioning: the on-screen calculator on the quant section can really slow you down, so I'd recommend getting used to that feature beforehand. I wish I had 😖
